title: GoThru Photo Studio Tauri UI Design

issues.main_description_html:
Stitch 360 Panorama - Enfuse-Style Editor Layout

Date: 2026-07-10
Status: Brainstorming spec
Audience: Claude with UI UX Pro Max
Branch: product-docs
Brainstorming: docs\superpowers\specs\2026-07-10-stitching-enfuse-layout-design.md

RESULT

Branch: UIUX-Update/stitching-360-image-layout

Goal

Redesign the Stitch 360 Panorama editor so it feels like the Enfuse editor. The page should use the same overall pattern: a large queue area on the left, a compact settings and FAQ panel on the right, and queue rows that can collapse and expand.

The redesign should make Stitch 360 easier to scan, easier to manage, and less space-heavy. It should keep all current stitching behavior, but present the queue and settings in a clearer Enfuse-style layout.

Main Layout

The editor has two main areas:

  1. Queue panel on the left.
  2. Settings and FAQ panel on the right.

The queue panel is always visible. It should not disappear when the queue is empty. When there are no queued panorama sets, show a small empty message inside the queue list area.

The right panel starts with Stitch 360 settings. The FAQ is available from the question/help button, following the same feeling as Enfuse.

Queue Header

The queue header should resemble the Enfuse queue header.

It includes:

  • Title: Stitch 360 Queue.
  • Counter summary: total sets, queued, processing, successful, failed, canceled, and incomplete.
  • Input location: the folder or selected image source used for the queue.
  • Output location: where the final Stitched folder will be created.
  • Add to Queue button.
  • Clear Queue button.
  • Stop All button, visible while stitching is running.

The output location line should be easy to read. If custom output is off, explain that results are saved beside the source images. If custom output is on, show the selected custom location.

Output Folder Rule

All Stitch 360 results are saved into one folder named Stitched.

If custom output is off:

  • Save results to <source folder>/Stitched.

If custom output is on:

  • Save results to <selected output location>/Stitched.

The queue header and settings should both make this rule clear without using technical wording.

Queue Set Row

Each row represents one panorama set.

The row contains:

  • Set sequence number, such as Set 1, Set 2, Set 3.
  • Panorama name.
  • Queue item status.
  • Expand or collapse button.
  • Selected image list.
  • Remove selected image controls, when allowed.
  • Control Point placeholder area.
  • Remove set item button, when allowed.
  • Status-specific action buttons.

The panorama name should be based on the first and last selected image in the set:

first_filename-last_filename-panorama.jpg

Example:

IMG_0001-IMG_0004-panorama.jpg

If there are six or eight images in a set, the name still uses the first and last image names.

Collapsed Row

When a queue row is collapsed, it shows only:

  • Panorama name.
  • Status.
  • Expand button.

This should match the simple scan-friendly behavior of Enfuse rows.

Expanded Row

When a queue row is expanded, it shows:

  • Panorama name.
  • Status.
  • Collapse button.
  • Selected image list.
  • Control Point placeholder.
  • Action buttons.

The selected image list shows the images in the set. For most users this will be four images, but it must also support six and eight images depending on the Photos per Panorama setting.

Queued and incomplete items may show remove controls for selected images. Processed items should not encourage changing the image list.

Control Point Placeholder

The Control Point area is a UI placeholder only in this spec.

It should appear for queue sets with these statuses:

  • Queued.
  • Failed.
  • Canceled.
  • Successful.

It does not need real control point editing, storage, or backend behavior yet.

The placeholder includes:

  • A linked control point list.
  • Each linked control point item shows a sequence number.
  • Each linked control point item has an edit linked control point icon.
  • An Add Control Point button.

The Add Control Point button and edit icons may open a placeholder modal, disabled state, or future-ready action depending on implementation preference. The important requirement is that the UI space and user flow are visible in the layout.

Queue Row Actions by Status

Queued

Show:

  • Remove set button.
  • Linked control point list.
  • Edit linked control point icon for each listed point.
  • Add Control Point button.

Queued sets are waiting to be stitched, so users can still adjust the set before processing starts.

Incomplete

Show:

  • Descriptive text explaining the set does not have enough images to stitch.
  • Remove set button.

Do not show retry or stitch actions for incomplete sets.

Processing

Show:

  • Short processing description.
  • Progress bar.
  • Cancel button.

Do not show image removal, retry, output, or control point actions while the set is actively processing.

Failed

Show:

  • Short failure description.
  • Retry button.
  • Retry with Layout button.
  • Control Point placeholder.

This gives the user a way to try again normally, try again with layout fallback, or prepare future control point adjustments.

Canceled

Show:

  • Short canceled description.
  • Retry button.
  • Retry with Layout button.
  • Control Point placeholder.

Canceled sets are treated like failed sets for recovery actions.

Successful

Show:

  • Retry button.
  • Retry with Layout button.
  • Open in 360 Viewer button.
  • Show in Folder button.
  • Control Point placeholder.

Successful rows should still allow retry because the user may want a better result with different layout handling later.

Settings Panel

The settings panel should be shorter, cleaner, and easier to read than the current Stitch 360 settings.

Use two sections:

  1. Basic Settings.
  2. Advanced Settings.

The settings should feel compact, with short labels and helpful descriptions only where they reduce confusion.

Basic Settings

Basic Settings includes:

  • Custom Output Location toggle.
  • Photos per Panorama radio buttons.
  • Lens Profile dropdown.
  • Output Width dropdown.

Custom Output Location

Use the same style as custom output location components in other edit modes.

When off:

  • Results are saved to the source folder's Stitched folder.

When on:

  • The user can choose a custom output location.
  • Results are saved to that location's Stitched folder.

Photos per Panorama

Use radio buttons:

  • 4 photos.
  • 6 photos.
  • 8 photos.

This setting controls how selected images are grouped into panorama sets.

Lens Profile

Use a dropdown for the supported lens profiles.

The label should stay simple: Lens Profile.

Output Width

Use a dropdown with title and description for each option:

  • Small (4096px): smaller file and faster processing.
  • High (8192px): default production-quality option.
  • Optimum: can produce very large files.

High should feel like the normal recommended choice.

Advanced Settings

Advanced Settings includes:

  • Roll Correction radio buttons.
  • Reuse Rig Alignment toggle.
  • Maximum features per image input.
  • Starting yaw degree input.
  • JPEG quality percentage input.

Roll Correction

Use radio buttons with short descriptions:

  • 0: keep each input photo as-is.
  • 90: rotate each input photo 90 degrees.
  • -90: rotate each input photo -90 degrees.

Reuse Rig Alignment

Use a toggle with a short description:

Reuse alignment from the first successful set for faster and more consistent results when every set was shot with the same rig.

This is still a queue-level setting. It does not create different alignment settings per set.

Maximum Features per Image

Use a number input.

Plain-language help text:

Controls how many visual points the stitcher can use from each photo. Higher values may help difficult images but can take longer.

Starting Yaw Degree

Use a number input.

Plain-language help text:

Rotates the starting direction of the finished panorama.

JPEG Quality

Use a percentage input.

Plain-language help text:

Higher quality creates larger files. Lower quality creates smaller files.

FAQ

The FAQ should use the same style as the Enfuse FAQ list, but the content is about 360 panorama stitching.

FAQ questions:

  1. What is 360 panorama stitching?
  2. How do I use 360 panorama stitching?
  3. What are the final results?
  4. Where are the results saved?

Suggested answers:

What is 360 panorama stitching?

360 panorama stitching combines a set of fisheye photos into one complete 360-degree panorama.

How do I use 360 panorama stitching?

Select the images for your panorama sets, choose how many photos belong in each panorama, confirm the lens and output settings, then add them to the queue and start stitching.

What are the final results?

Each complete set creates one equirectangular panorama image that can be opened in the 360 viewer.

Where are the results saved?

Results are saved in a folder named Stitched. If custom output is off, the folder is created beside the source images. If custom output is on, the folder is created inside the selected output location.

Empty Queue State

When the queue is empty, keep the Enfuse-style queue card visible.

Show a short message:

Select panorama photos, then click Add to Queue.

The empty state should not be a large landing page. It should be a quiet message inside the queue list area.

Out of Scope

This spec does not include real control point editing.

Out of scope:

  • Saving control points.
  • Editing control point coordinates.
  • Passing control point data into the stitcher.
  • Changing the backend stitch process.
  • Changing the actual queue processing behavior.
  • Adding per-set stitching settings.

The Control Point feature in this spec is only a visible layout placeholder so the interface is ready for a future control point workflow.

Success Criteria

The redesign is successful when:

  • Stitch 360 visually resembles the Enfuse editor.
  • The queue header shows title, counters, input location, output location, and queue actions.
  • Queue rows can collapse and expand.
  • Collapsed rows are simple and easy to scan.
  • Expanded rows show selected images, control point placeholder, and status-specific actions.
  • Settings are shorter and grouped into Basic and Advanced sections.
  • Output behavior clearly points to a single Stitched folder.
  • FAQ content is written for Stitch 360 users.
  • The wording is simple enough for non-technical users.

issues.display_title: Issue #69: Create Stitch 360 Control Point Page Layout
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT

Branch: UIUX-Update/stitching-360-image-layout

Summary

Create the Stitch 360 Panorama Control Point page layout described in the brainstorming spec.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-stitching-control-point-layout-design.md

Goal

When a user clicks Edit Linked Control Point or Add Control Point from a Stitch 360 queue set, open a full Control Point workspace inside the main app window. The page should help users compare two source images from the selected panorama set and mark matching control points between them.

Layout Requirements

  • Page opens inside the main app window, replacing the Stitch 360 queue/settings view.
  • Header includes:
    • Panorama/set name.
    • Action buttons.
    • Mode-sensitive instructions.
    • Close button returning to the Stitch 360 queue.
  • Body uses three panels:
    • Flat Viewer 1: 40%.
    • Flat Viewer 2: 40%.
    • Control Point List: 20%.

Header Actions

  • Add Control Point toggle.
  • Delete Control Point toggle.
  • Link Scroll toggle.
  • Save as JSON.
  • Import Control Point.
  • Clear All Control Points with confirmation modal.

Interaction Requirements

  • Add and Delete modes are mutually exclusive.
  • Link Scroll synchronizes vertical scroll, horizontal scroll, and zoom between both viewers.
  • Each viewer has an image dropdown and flat image display.
  • Viewer 1 and Viewer 2 cannot show the same image at the same time.
  • Add mode guides the user to pick a point in one viewer, then the matching point in the other viewer.
  • Add mode shows a zoomed hover preview near the cursor.
  • Completed points appear in both viewers with matching number and color.
  • Delete mode removes a clicked point from both viewers and the list.
  • The Control Point List shows Viewer 1 file name, Viewer 2 file name, point number, pixel distance, and delete action.

Out of Scope

  • Passing control points into the stitching engine.
  • Changing the stitching algorithm.
  • Replacing automatic alignment.
  • Building advanced control point optimization.
  • Editing point coordinates in a form.
  • Supporting more than two viewers at the same time.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Control Point page opens from the Stitch 360 queue set control point actions.
  • Page is inside the main app window, not a separate Tauri window and not a small modal.
  • Header, action buttons, instructions, and close behavior match the spec.
  • 40/40/20 panel layout is implemented.
  • Viewer dropdowns prevent selecting the same image in both viewers.
  • Add/Delete modes cannot both be active.
  • Link Scroll synchronizes both viewers when active.
  • Save, Import, and Clear All actions are present and understandable.
  • Clear All shows a confirmation modal.
  • Empty and error states use plain language.
